newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo bourse says hopes to start stock options.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo bourse says hopes to start stock options.

text.p: The president of the Tokyo Stock Exchange, Mitsuhide Yamaguchi, told reporters on Tuesday that the bourse hopes to list individual stock options next year.
"We see the necessity to list individual stock options on our exchange and want to study details of the listings as soon as possible," Yamaguchi said.
He said that an advisory panel to the finance minister recently announced that Japan should introduce trading of individual stock options.
Japan's securities industry has also urged that the trading be allowed.

Asked how the Tokyo exchange will cooperate with the Osaka Securities Exchange, which has also been planning to list individual stock options, Yamaguchi said the Tokyo exchange will discuss how it plans to list the options with Osaka because it is better to have the same listing procedures and rules.
While it introduced stock index futures and options in the late 1980s, the Finance Ministry has taken a cautious approach on options for individual stocks.

Yamaguchi also told a regular news conference that the exchange expects Chinese companies to list their shares, and that the bourse would try to create an environment to attract Japanese investors to those shares.

He also said the exchange was looking at the listing of holding companies in light of the the recent agreement between Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp (NTT) and the Posts Ministry to break up the telecommunications giant under a holding company, which have been banned in Japan since 1947.
"We are very much interested in the introduction of a holding company system and will start studying the listing of holding companies," he said.
